proof.text: The given kernel arrow $k$ is a monomorphism: if $ka=kb$ for $a,b:T\to K$, then $ka$ is annihilated by $d$ and both $a$ and $b$ are factorizations through the given kernel. Its uniqueness clause gives $a=b$.

source.place: Tag 05QU, proof of (1) implies (3), the kernel inclusion is a monomorphism

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-pretriangulated-monomorphisms-split] to $k$ to choose $r_0:X\to K$ with $r_0k=1_K$. By TR1 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] complete $k$ to a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{k}X\xrightarrow{p}Z\xrightarrow{h}K[1]$. Its twice-rotated triangle starts with $h$ followed by $-k[1]$. Clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $k[1]h=0$. Composing by $r_0[1]$ gives $h=0$, since $(r_0k)[1]=1_{K[1]}$. Now [lem-pc-derived-zero-third-split] gives $e:X\xrightarrow{\sim}K\oplus Z$ with $ek=i_K$ and $p=p_Ze$. Write $r=p_Ke:X\to K$ and $s=e^{-1}i_Z:Z\to X$. The biproduct equations of [def-weil-additive-category] give
$$rk=1_K,\quad pk=0,\quad ps=1_Z,\quad kr+sp=1_X.$$

source.place: Tag 05QU, first monomorphism splitting in proof (1) implies (3); preceding lemma-split for the compatible biproduct triangle

proof.text: Put $g=ds:Z\to Y$. Multiplying $kr+sp=1_X$ by $d$, and using $dk=0$, gives $d=gp$. To prove $g$ monic, suppose $ga=0$ for $a:T\to Z$. Then $dsa=0$, so the given kernel supplies $b:T\to K$ with $sa=kb$. Applying $p$ gives $a=psa=pkb=0$. If $ga_1=ga_2$, apply this to $a_1-a_2$ to obtain $a_1=a_2$; subtraction and bilinearity are available by [def-weil-preadditive-category]. Thus [lem-sfb-pretriangulated-monomorphisms-split] supplies $t:Y\to Z$ with $tg=1_Z$. In particular $td=tgp=p$.

source.place: Tag 05QU, proof (1) implies (3), the restricted map on the complementary summand is monic and splits

proof.text:
Apply $F$ to the identities $rk=1_K$, $kr+sp=1_X$, $td=p$, and $dk=0$. Functoriality preserves compositions and identities, while [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] preserves sums and zero. Thus $F(d)F(k)=0$. For any object $T$ of $\mathcal D$ and arrow $a:T\to F(X)$ satisfying $F(d)a=0$, one has
$$F(p)a=F(t)F(d)a=0,$$
$$a=(F(k)F(r)+F(s)F(p))a=F(k)(F(r)a).$$
Here bilinearity is [def-weil-preadditive-category]. Hence $b=F(r)a$ is a factorization through $F(k)$. If $F(k)b'=a$, then $b'=F(r)F(k)b'=F(r)a=b$. This is the required universal property. The object $T$ is arbitrary in $\mathcal D$, and no other kernel, biproduct, or limit is assumed to exist there.

title: Additive functors from a pre-triangulated category preserve existing kernels
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] and $\mathcal D$ a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. For any morphism $d:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal C$ and any kernel $k:K\to X$ of $d$, $F(k):F(K)\to F(X)$ is a kernel of $F(d)$. Here a kernel of $d$ means $dk=0$ and that every $a:T\to X$ with $da=0$ factors uniquely as $a=kb$ with $b:T\to K$. No existence of other kernels in either category is assumed.
